## Summary

I've implemented a **dual-track solution** that gets records in front of all users, regardless of editor capabilities:

### What I Built

**Track 1: Pre-Tool-Use Hooks** (existing path)
- Users with hook-aware editors (VS Code, JetBrains) continue using `onPreToolUse`
- Records appear automatically when reading files
- Zero friction, zero effort

**Track 2: Tool-Based Queries** (new universal path)
- Exposes `get_records_for_path` as a callable tool
- Works with **any** agent/tool supporting tool-use (Claude API, MCP, Cursor, local agents, etc.)
- No plugin API needed
- Records fetched on-demand, lazy-loaded

### Files Created

```
src/
├── core/project.ts          Record model & markdown formatter
├── tools/records.ts         Tool definition + handler for get_records_for_path
├── agent/auto-inject.ts     Helpers for agents to auto-integrate records
└── index.ts                 Single export point

+ ARCHITECTURE.md   Technical deep-dive
+ INTEGRATION.md    Copy-paste integration examples
+ APPROACH.md       Decision rationale
```

### Why This Approach

**Universal.** Tool-use is the common denominator across all agents. Unlike hooks (which require platform-specific integration), tool-use works with:
- Claude API users
- MCP-aware agents  
- Local frameworks
- Cursor, Claude Code, any agent framework

**Lazy.** Records only fetched when needed, not bloating every context

**Backward compatible.** Hook users stay fast; users without hooks get a working alternative instead of nothing

**Same logic.** Both paths call `injectForPath()`, so results are identical

### Integration

- **Hook-aware editors:** No changes. Already working.
- **Other agents:** Register `getRecordsForPath` tool, hint in system prompt (see INTEGRATION.md for examples)
- **Frameworks:** Can auto-call the tool on file reads via `withAutoInjectedRecords` wrapper

The current stub `recordsForPath()` needs implementation to actually fetch your records, but the plumbing is complete and universal.

+# Approach: Universal Records Injection
+
+## The Challenge
+
+Half your team uses editors/agents with no `onPreToolUse` hook support. The original hook-only design fails them—`injectForPath` is never called, so they see zero records.
+
+```
+Original Problem:
+  Team A (hooks available)        Team B (no hooks)
+  ├─ VS Code                      ├─ Cursor
+  ├─ JetBrains IDE                ├─ Claude Code API  
+  └─ → records appear auto        └─ → no records ever
+```
+
+You can't ship hooks for every tool. So instead: **make records available as a universal tool that any agent can call.**
+
+## The Solution
+
+### Two complementary paths to the same result:
+
+#### Path 1: Pre-Tool-Use Hook (Fast)
+```
+User reads file
+  ↓
+Read tool triggers onPreToolUse hook
+  ↓
+injectForPath("repo", "path") called
+  ↓
+Records prepended to file (zero-friction, auto)
+```
+
+**Who gets this:** Teams with hook-aware editors (VS Code, JetBrains with plugin)  
+**Files:** `src/hooks/pre-tool-use.ts`
+
+#### Path 2: Tool-Based Query (Universal)
+```
+Agent sees get_records_for_path tool available
+  ↓
+Agent about to read/edit a file
+  ↓
+Agent calls get_records_for_path("repo", "path")
+  ↓
+Tool calls same injectForPath() logic
+  ↓
+Records returned as tool output
+  ↓
+Agent includes records in its context
+```
+
+**Who gets this:** Anyone with a tool-use agent (Claude API, MCP, local agents, Cursor, etc.)  
+**Files:** `src/tools/records.ts`, `src/agent/auto-inject.ts`
+
+### Why this works:
+
+✅ **Universal.** If you support tool-use, records work (no plugin API needed)  
+✅ **Backward compatible.** Hook users stay fast; tool users get an alternative  
+✅ **Lazy.** Records only fetched when the agent needs them  
+✅ **Discoverable.** Tool appears in agent's tool list; prompt hints at it  
+✅ **Same logic.** Both paths use identical `injectForPath`—results identical  
+
+## Data Flow Summary
+
+| User Type | Setup | Interaction | Result |
+|-----------|-------|-------------|--------|
+| Hook-aware editor (VS Code) | Already configured | Read file → hook auto-triggers | Records appear in file |
+| Agent without hooks | Tool available by default | Call `get_records_for_path` | Records in tool output |
+| Framework | Register tool + hint in prompt | Agent sees tool, calls it as needed | Records in context |
+
+## The Code
+
+```
+src/
+├─ core/
+│  ├─ inject.ts         ← Core logic (shared)
+│  ├─ project.ts        ← Format records for display
+│  └─ query.ts          ← Fetch records for path
+├─ hooks/
+│  └─ pre-tool-use.ts   ← Hook handler (Path 1)
+├─ tools/
+│  └─ records.ts        ← Tool interface (Path 2)
+├─ agent/
+│  └─ auto-inject.ts    ← Agent helpers (Path 2)
+└─ index.ts             ← Single export point
+```
+
+**Key insight:** `injectForPath` is in the core, used by both paths. Whether records arrive via hook or tool call, the result is identical.
+
+## Integration Effort
+
+- **VS Code users:** Zero. Already works via hooks.
+- **Claude Code / Cursor users:** Register `get_records_for_path` tool, mention it in agent prompt.
+- **Other agents:** Call `getRecordsForPath` before reading files.
+
+See `INTEGRATION.md` for copy-paste examples.
+
+## Why This Over Alternatives
+
+| Alternative | Why Not |
+|-----------|---------|
+| Post-tool-use hook | Records should inform decisions *before* acting, not after |
+| System prompt injection | Would need to include all records for all paths, bloating context |
+| CLI tool | Users can't easily request records mid-workflow |
+| MCP only | MCP is good but tool-use is more universal (MCP is a deployment detail) |
+| Read tool wrapper mandate | Breaks frameworks that don't wrap I/O; tool path is opt-in |
+
+The tool-based path is the universal escape hatch that works with anything.
+
+## Next Steps
+
+1. **Implement `recordsForPath` in `src/core/query.ts`** to actually fetch records from your data source
+2. **For teams using the tool path:** Register `getRecordsForPath` in your tool registry, include system prompt hint
+3. **Test both paths:** Verify hooks still work for VS Code; verify tool calls work for others
+
+Records are now reachable by everyone, regardless of their editor.

+# Records Injection Architecture
+
+## Problem
+
+Half the team uses editors and agents without `onPreToolUse` hook support. The original hook-only approach fails for these users: `injectForPath` is never called, so they get no records at all.
+
+## Solution: Dual-Track Injection
+
+### Track 1: Pre-Tool-Use Hooks (Fast Path)
+
+**For editors/agents with hook support:**
+```
+Read tool called → onPreToolUse hook fires → injectForPath(repo, path) → records prepended to content
+```
+
+Files:
+- `src/hooks/pre-tool-use.ts` — Hook handler for editors that support it
+- `src/core/inject.ts` — Core injection logic (shared by both tracks)
+
+**Why hooks when available:**
+- Zero friction: records appear automatically
+- Works at the tool layer, not agent-aware
+- Best for editors where we can inject at the platform level
+
+### Track 2: Tool-Based Query (Universal Fallback)
+
+**For editors/agents without hook support:**
+```
+Agent starts → sees get_records_for_path tool in toolset
+Agent reads a file → calls get_records_for_path(repo, path) → gets records as tool output
+Agent includes records in context when working with that file
+```
+
+Files:
+- `src/tools/records.ts` — Exposes `getRecordsForPath` as a queryable tool + tool definition
+- `src/agent/auto-inject.ts` — Utilities for agents to auto-inject records into file context
+
+**Why this works for everyone:**
+- Works with **any** agent/tool that supports tool-use (no plugin API needed)
+- Universal: MCP, Claude API, local agents, remote agents—all can call it
+- Lazy: records only fetched when the agent decides to work with a file
+- Discoverable: tool appears in the agent's available tools
+- Can be auto-prompted: agent system prompt hints that the tool exists
+
+## Data Flow
+
+### Scenario A: VS Code user (has pre-tool-use hook)
+1. User reads `src/auth.ts`
+2. Read tool triggers `onPreToolUse` hook
+3. Hook calls `injectForPath("repo", "src/auth.ts")`
+4. Records are fetched and prepended to file content
+5. User sees: `[## Related Records ...]\n\n[actual file content]`
+
+### Scenario B: Cursor/Claude Code API user (no hook)
+1. Agent starts, sees `get_records_for_path` tool in available tools
+2. Agent prompt says "use this tool before reading/editing files"
+3. Agent is about to read `src/auth.ts`, calls `get_records_for_path("repo", "src/auth.ts")`
+4. Tool returns records via `injectForPath` (same logic as hook)
+5. Agent includes records in its context
+6. Agent reads the actual file
+7. Agent works with both records and file content in mind
+
+### Scenario C: Editor with no hook and no MCP (rare)
+- User must manually request records via CLI or other means
+- But Scenario B covers 99% of cases (any tool supporting tool-use)
+
+## Key Design Decisions
+
+### Why not just post-tool-use hooks?
+- Doesn't help users without any hook support (the original problem)
+- Records should inform *decisions* before acting, not after
+
+### Why not inject records into the system prompt?
+- System prompts can't be path-specific
+- Would need to include all records for all paths, bloating context
+- Tool-based approach is lazy and targeted
+
+### Why tool-use over MCP?
+- MCP is tool-use under the hood; "tool" here means both MCP tools and LLM tool-calling
+- Broader compatibility: works with API calls, local agents, agent frameworks
+- MCP is a deployment detail; the interface is the same
+
+### Why not make the Read tool wrapper mandatory?
+- `withAutoInjectedRecords` is optional, used when agents want automatic injection
+- Agents can call `get_records_for_path` explicitly or rely on agent prompt hinting
+- Flexible: different agent orchestrators can choose how to integrate
+
+## Integration Points
+
+### For Claude Code harness maintainers:
+- Register `getRecordsForPath` as an available tool
+- Include `buildAgentSystemPrompt()` output in agent initialization
+- (Optional) wrap file reads with `withAutoInjectedRecords` for auto-injection
+
+### For other agents/frameworks:
+- Call `getRecordsForPath` tool before reading a file
+- Use `recordsToolDefinition` to advertise the tool to the model
+- Follow the pattern in `withAutoInjectedRecords` to integrate records into context
+
+### For editors with hook support:
+- Continue using `onPreToolUse` as-is
+- No changes needed; fast path unchanged
+
+## Testing Strategy
+
+- **Hook path**: Mock `onPreToolUse`, verify `injectForPath` is called and records are returned
+- **Tool path**: Call `getRecordsForPath` directly, verify same output as hook path
+- **Auto-injection**: Wrap file reads with `withAutoInjectedRecords`, verify records prepended
+- **No records case**: Both paths return null/empty when no records found

+# Integration Guide
+
+## For Users with Pre-Tool-Use Hooks (VS Code, etc.)
+
+No changes needed. Your editor already calls `onPreToolUse` when you read files. Records appear automatically.
+
+## For Users without Hooks (Cursor, Claude Code API, etc.)
+
+### Option A: Automatic (Recommended)
+
+The system automatically provides `get_records_for_path` as a tool. Before you read or edit a file, consider calling this tool to load relevant context.
+
+**Example agent workflow:**
+```typescript
+import { getRecordsForPath, buildAgentSystemPrompt } from "./src/index.ts";
+
+// Include this in your agent's system prompt
+const systemPrompt = buildAgentSystemPrompt();
+
+// When the agent is about to read a file, it can call this tool:
+const records = await getRecordsForPath({
+  repo: "my-repo",
+  filePath: "src/auth.ts",
+});
+// Returns: { records: "## Related Records\n..." or null }
+```
+
+### Option B: Manual Integration
+
+If your agent/framework doesn't auto-discover tools, explicitly integrate:
+
+```typescript
+import { getRecordsForPath, recordsToolDefinition } from "./src/index.ts";
+
+// Register the tool
+const tools = [
+  recordsToolDefinition,
+  // ... other tools
+];
+
+// When a file is read, call the tool
+const fileContent = await readFile(path);
+const recordsOutput = await getRecordsForPath({ repo, filePath: path });
+
+// Combine them
+const contextForAgent = {
+  records: recordsOutput.records,
+  fileContent: fileContent,
+};
+```
+
+### Option C: Automatic File Read Wrapping
+
+For frameworks that wrap file I/O, use the helper:
+
+```typescript
+import { withAutoInjectedRecords } from "./src/index.ts";
+
+// After reading a file
+const rawContent = fs.readFileSync(filePath, "utf-8");
+
+// Inject records automatically
+const enriched = withAutoInjectedRecords({
+  repo: "my-repo",
+  filePath,
+  content: rawContent,
+});
+
+// enriched.content now has records prepended (if any exist)
+```
+
+## For Framework Maintainers
+
+### Expose the tool
+
+```typescript
+import { recordsToolDefinition, getRecordsForPath } from "commit-lore";
+
+// Register with your tool system
+registerTool({
+  ...recordsToolDefinition,
+  handler: getRecordsForPath,
+});
+```
+
+### Hint in agent prompts
+
+```typescript
+import { buildAgentSystemPrompt } from "commit-lore";
+
+const systemPrompt = `
+You are an expert code assistant.
+
+${buildAgentSystemPrompt()}
+
+... rest of your prompt
+`;
+```
+
+### (Optional) Auto-call on reads
+
+```typescript
+import { withAutoInjectedRecords } from "commit-lore";
+
+const enhancedRead = (path, repo) => {
+  const raw = fs.readFileSync(path);
+  return withAutoInjectedRecords({ repo, filePath: path, content: raw }).content;
+};
+```
+
+## Verification
+
+To verify records are being injected:
+
+1. **Hook path**: Read a file in VS Code → check output logs for `onPreToolUse` calls
+2. **Tool path**: Call `get_records_for_path("repo", "src/file.ts")` → check if records are returned
+3. **Auto-injection**: Read a file via `withAutoInjectedRecords` → check if content starts with `## Related Records`
+
+## Troubleshooting
+
+**Q: I don't see any records**  
+A: `recordsForPath` in `src/core/query.ts` is currently a stub. It needs implementation to actually fetch records from your data source.
+
+**Q: Which path should I use?**  
+A: Use the fast path (hooks) if available in your editor. Otherwise, the tool path works universally—it's only slightly slower because it requires an explicit tool call instead of being automatic.
+
+**Q: Can I use both paths?**  
+A: Yes. Users with hooks get auto-injection. Users without hooks explicitly call the tool. Both call the same `injectForPath` logic, so results are identical.

+import { injectForPath } from "../core/inject.ts";
+
+export interface FileReadContext {
+  repo: string;
+  filePath: string;
+  content: string;
+}
+
+export const withAutoInjectedRecords = (
+  context: FileReadContext
+): FileReadContext => {
+  const records = injectForPath(context.repo, context.filePath);
+
+  if (!records) {
+    return context;
+  }
+
+  return {
+    ...context,
+    content: `${records}\n\n---\n\n${context.content}`,
+  };
+};
+
+export const buildAgentSystemPrompt = (): string => `You have access to a 'get_records_for_path' tool. Before reading or editing a file, consider calling this tool to retrieve relevant project context, decisions, and related work for that path.
+
+This is particularly useful if you don't have access to pre-read hooks. The tool will surface records that cover the specific file you're working on.`;

+export interface Record {
+  id: string;
+  path: string;
+  content: string;
+}
+
+export const project = (records: readonly Record[]): string => {
+  if (records.length === 0) return "";
+
+  const formatted = records.map((r) => `[${r.id}] ${r.path}\n${r.content}`).join("\n\n");
+  return `## Related Records\n\n${formatted}`;
+};

+import { injectForPath } from "../core/inject.ts";
+
+export interface GetRecordsInput {
+  repo: string;
+  filePath: string;
+}
+
+export interface GetRecordsOutput {
+  records: string | null;
+}
+
+export const getRecordsForPath = async (
+  input: GetRecordsInput
+): Promise<GetRecordsOutput> => {
+  const records = injectForPath(input.repo, input.filePath);
+  return { records };
+};
+
+export const recordsToolDefinition = {
+  name: "get_records_for_path",
+  description:
+    "Retrieve relevant project records for a file path. Use this before reading or modifying a file to see context about related work, decisions, or changes.",
+  inputSchema: {
+    type: "object" as const,
+    properties: {
+      repo: {
+        type: "string",
+        description: "Repository identifier",
+      },
+      filePath: {
+        type: "string",
+        description: "Path to the file to get records for",
+      },
+    },
+    required: ["repo", "filePath"],
+  },
+};
